instruction: Reorder your favorites so that Vim appears first, followed by Chrome, then Thunderbird.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires reordering favorite apps to a specific sequence. Uses custom metric that checks order, not just set membership. Expected order: vim, chrome, thunderbird.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator logic is semantically correct and can properly verify the instruction: getter extracts favorite apps order via gsettings command, metric compares exact order, expected values match instruction requirements (Vim first, Chrome second, Thunderbird third)
Complete coverage: evaluator checks all three apps in the exact required order

Metric function has good implementation quality: uses ast.literal_eval() for safe parsing (not eval()), includes error handling for malformed output and type validation, validates that expected apps are present before checking order
Comparison logic is appropriate: uses exact list equality to verify order matches exactly as instructed
State extraction is appropriate: gsettings command directly reads GNOME shell favorite-apps setting, no UI state dependency (the static warning about UI dependency is a false positive)
Will work correctly at runtime: metric tries expected.get('expected_order') first which will succeed when framework passes rules dict directly
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Metric function line 28 shows conceptual misunderstanding: fallback pattern 'expected.get("rules", {}).get("expected_order", [])' is incorrect. When expected.type='rule', framework passes rules dict directly (not {rules: {...}}). Should only use: expected.get('expected_order', [])
Remove the incorrect fallback pattern to avoid confusion. Current code works because first attempt succeeds, but the fallback logic is wrong
